I don't want to be pushed into war by Israel, and I don't want to be in a war with Iran. I want our money spent here to buy schools and health care and child care here. I don't understand why that is so inconceivable.
Al-Sayed's debate in Grand Rapids with former Republican Congressman Mike Rogers was a combative affair. In Georgia, Democratic Senator John Ossoff squared off with his Republican challenger, Congressman Mike Collins, who sought to make immigration an issue.
Illegal immigrants, though, that John Ossoff led into this country, not only were coming over here killing people and murdering people like Lake and Raleigh, and he wouldn't shut the door on it. Human trafficking that he just let continue to flow.

Collins sponsored the Lake and Raleigh Act, the 2025 law named for a Georgia nursing student killed by a Venezuelan man in the U.S. illegally.
Ossoff said Collins should answer for President Trump's deportation campaign. Mortgage rates up again this week. The national average for a 30-year fixed rate loan is 7.4 percent, NPR's Stephen Bassaha.
It wasn't that long ago, back in February, when mortgage rates had fallen below 6 percent. But since then, two major events have caused a sharp jump in the costs of borrowing, including for a house.
The first was the start of the U.S. and Israeli war against Iran. That caused investors to worry about inflation, which caused bond yields to rise.
The second event was the Federal Reserve raising interest rates last month to fight that inflation. Rates quickly climbed past 7 percent, and they've kept climbing since.
The Fed will meet later this month to decide on whether to again hike rates, which could drive mortgage rates up even higher. Stephen Bassaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
The Southern Rail Commission closing Amtrak's Mardi Gras service from New Orleans to Mobile, Alabama, as the Gulf Coast prepares for Hurricane Isaias. From member station WRKF, Brooke Thorrington has more.
Ahead of the storm, the Army Corps of Engineers is closing the New Orleans floodgates to protect the Crescent City from any storm surge.
Chairman of the Southern Rail Commission Knox Ross says when that happens, it blocks the track so service has to be rerouted.
That's why we've replaced one of the trains with a bus. In events like this, we've had this happen before, where they close the floodgates and just prevents the train from running.
Amtrak service between New Orleans and Atlanta is also impacted. It's temporarily canceled. Affected passengers can check their Amtrak app for updates along with social media.
Services for both routes are expected to be back on track Monday. For NPR News, I'm Brooke Thorrington and Baton Rouge.
And you're listening to NPR News. Demonstrators clashed with police in New York City outside a hospital where a man shot Thursday by federal immigration officers was being treated.
The whole man's security department says a shooting happened in the course of a targeted enforcement operation.

Candidates to be Alaska's next governor squared off in a debate last night. It's a four-way ranked choice race under Alaska's unique voting system.
Alaska public media's Eric Stone reports a current governor's term limit.
Three Republicans are facing off against a Democrat in the race to be Alaska's next governor. Democrat Jonathan Christ Tompkins has a lead over the fractured Republican field. He's positioning himself as a pragmatic moderate.
We need to be able to work together to find common ground, to bridge where there's disagreement, and that's what's going to move Alaska forward.
The top polling Republican is business owner Bernadette Wilson. She said she'd fight efforts to raise taxes on oil companies as Alaska stares down to budget crunch.
I am up for that battle. I do not want a governor that's going to concede the fight before they even get started.

For NPR News, I'm Eric Stone in Anchorage.
